items.label: section_header
items.text: REACTIONS WITH WATER

items.label: text
items.text: All these metals react in the same way with water to produce a metal hydroxide and hydrogen:

items.label: formula
items.text: \ a l k a l i \, \text {metal} + \text {water} \to \ a l k a l i \, \text {metal} \, \text {hydroxide} + \text {hydrogen} \\ 2 M \quad + 2 H _ { 2 } O \to \quad 2 M O H \quad + \quad H _ { 2 }

items.label: text
items.text: The main difference between the reactions is how quickly they happen.

items.label: text
items.text: As you go down the group, the metals become more reactive and the reactions occur more rapidly.

items.label: text
items.text: The reaction between sodium and water is typical.

items.label: section_header
items.text: WITH SODIUM

items.label: text
items.text: 2Na(s) + 2H₂O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + H2(g)

items.label: text
items.text: Strictly speaking, most of the time the sodium is reacting it is present as molten sodium, not solid sodium. Writing (l) for the state symbol has the potential to confuse an examiner and is probably best avoided! items.text: HINT

items.label: text
items.text: When asked to write observations in the exam it is better to write 'fizzing/ bubbling/effervescing' rather than 'a gas is given off' because the fizzing/ bubbling/effervescing is what you actually see.

items.label: caption
items.text: Figure 11.6 A hovercraft

items.label: list_item
items.text: Figure 11.5 Sodium reacting with water. The white trail is the sodium hydroxide, which dissolves in water to form a strongly alkaline solution.

items.label: text
items.text: The main observations you can make when this reaction occurs are:

items.label: list_item
items.text: The sodium floats because it is less dense than water.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The sodium melts into a ball because its melting point is low and a lot of heat is produced by the reaction.

items.label: list_item
items.text: There is fizzing because hydrogen gas is produced.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The sodium moves around on the surface of the water. Because the hydrogen isn't given off symmetrically around the ball, the sodium is pushed around the surface of the water, like a hovercraft.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The piece of sodium gets smaller and eventually disappears. The sodium is used up in the reaction.

items.label: list_item
items.text: If you test the solution that is formed with universal indicator solution, you will see that the universal indicator goes blue, indicating an alkaline solution has been formed. The metal hydroxide is alkaline (the solution contains the OH- ion).
